A1.justification: Both complete, readable 19-page PDFs describe the same LA-CDM research. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison cover all sections, equations, six figures, six tables, and Appendices A–E without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original LA-CDM evaluations on MIMIC-CDM, including diagnostic performance, calibration, ablations, qualitative examples, and Appendix D cost-sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3 and 6, calibration results, and the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The two-agent architecture, shared model weights, iterative test-request procedure, supervised hypothesis training, and GRPO calibration and action-training objectives are identical in Sections 3–4 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIMIC-CDM for sequential diagnosis of the same four abdominal conditions. Both retain the simulated inter-institutional pricing variation and expensive-CBC scenarios in Appendix D.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparators: OASST, SFT-all, SM-DDPO, ReAct, and LA-CDM (ZS). The qualifications concerning OASST's different evaluation setting and SM-DDPO's tabular-only inputs are unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 5 and Appendix C retain identical preprocessing, the 80/10/10 data split, model configuration, training settings, and accuracy, F1, ECE, and cost metrics. Appendix D's price-variation protocols are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the test-cost reward ablation in Table 2, hypothesis-agent ablation in Table 3, successful and failed diagnostic examples in Figures 4–6, and both cost-sensitivity analyses in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The existing point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 1 reports LA-CDM mean accuracy of 81.3 and average test cost of $1295.61 in both; Appendix D retains the same cost-variation results and CBC-request reduction from 19.2% to 2.5%.

T1.justification: The policy and state definitions, confidence-calibration mathematics, formal agent mappings, and diagnosis and test-cost reward equations in Sections 3–4 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about explicitly training hypothesis-driven clinical decision-making, improving diagnostic accuracy and efficiency, and enabling patient-adaptive testing.

C2.justification: Interpretations of calibration, testing efficiency, and patient-adaptive behavior are unchanged. Both retain the retrospective-data and missing-test limitations in Section 6 and the overconfidence-related failure interpretation in Appendix B.

D1.justification: Appendix A's prompts, Appendix C's preprocessing, LoRA settings, training schedule, hardware and training-time disclosures, and the code-access statements are identical. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning are unchanged. The new conference-publication header does not revise the scientific relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 replaces 'Preprint.' with 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026', reverses the order of Matthias Keicher and Nassir Navab, and removes their shared-last-authorship note. Scientific wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The running header and first-page author block change. Removing the authorship footnote causes limited text reflow and spacing changes across pages 1–4. All figures and tables retain their graphics, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information are identical across both PDFs, including the appendices. Publication and authorship edits with minor pagination changes provide no meaningful improvement or deterioration in the paper's overall quality.
